label: copy-phase input token f (from 3rd copy step on)
explanation: Token detector for the letter f being fed back as input during the copy phase. Fires essentially only when in_tok == f and phase == copy (recall 99.96%, mass recall 99.99% for that broad predicate); never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on any other input token (a few negligible r activations). Within copy-phase f inputs it is mostly silent at the first copy-phase input step (recall_idx 1), so restricting to recall_idx >= 2 gives the best F1. Magnitude is largest when f is the 3rd original token (input at recall_idx 2, right after the first post-DEL copy), and for a repeated f the second f is weaker; when f sits early (orig 0) or is the last input it is weak or silent. Does not depend on output token or other history.

issues: The test scores reproduce: P 0.927, R 0.934, F1 0.931, mass recall 0.980. On dev the broad predicate (phase 2, input f) scores P 0.807, R 0.9996, F1 0.893, mass recall 0.9999. All activation is in the copy phase: the original phase and the delimiter have 0 active steps, and the only activation on another input token is 31 steps on r.

The recall_idx == 1 cutoff is soft, not a clean boundary. When f is fed back at recall_idx 1, the feature still fires 28% of the time (precision 0.28, 16650 steps), but weakly: 22% of the lowest-quartile activations and 1.9% of mass. Most misses on test are this case (rendered as 'f ... <DEL> [f:0.04-0.18]').

The label and explanation leave out a decay with position. Precision of 'input f in copy phase' by recall_idx is 0.99 at 2, 1.00 at 3, 0.95 at 4, 0.84 at 5, 0.80 at 6, 0.84 at 7 and 0.89 at 8. By to_go it goes from 0.88 at 0 to 1.00 at 5. Late f inputs often fall below threshold, so the false positives are a graded fade, not a separate class.

The claim that other history has 'little effect' is somewhat overstated. For f at recall_idx >= 4, precision depends on prev_tok: z 0.46, e 0.60, f 0.66, u 0.73, against 1.0 for a, i, l and y. It also depends on out_tok: v 0.60, w 0.63, q 0.76. The effect is spread over many tokens. Excluding prev_tok in {z, e, f} at recall_idx >= 4 raises test precision to 0.947 but lowers F1 to 0.923, so no simple fix beats the predicate.

Other refinements also failed to beat the predicate. Adding 'not the first f' lowered dev F1 to 0.920, requiring to_go >= 1 lowered it to 0.825, and adding back recall_idx 1 when L <= 4 lowered test F1 to 0.916. The magnitude claims hold: top activations are f at recall_idx 2, and the second of two adjacent f's is weaker (0.27-0.49 of max).
